title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Ignore the reason for the visit. Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint
Chronic cough and shortness of breath.

HPI
The patient is a 68-year-old male presenting for evaluation of a persistent dry cough that has worsened over the last two weeks. He reports increased fatigue and mild wheezing when exerting himself. He denies fever, chills, or chest pain. He states that his breathing feels more labored during his morning walks. He has been using a rescue inhaler with minimal relief.

Medication List
Lisinopril 20mg, Metoprolol succinate 50mg, Albuterol HFA, Atorvastatin 40mg, Furosemide 40mg.

Exam
Vital signs are stable. Respiratory effort is increased; lungs show scattered wheezing in the upper lobes. Heart sounds are regular with an S3 and S4 gallop. No peripheral edema noted in the lower extremities. Patient appears mildly distressed but is in no acute respiratory crisis.

Assessment
1. Acute exacerbation of chronic cough.
2. Shortness of breath.

Plan
1. Order chest X-ray and pulmonary function tests.
2. Start a trial of a short-acting bronchodilator.
3. Follow up in one week to assess progress.
explanations: Heart-failure medications on the list do not establish the diagnosis; coders do not infer diagnoses from medications.

distractors.why: Only the provider can document a diagnosis.
